summary: Stringozzi (or linguine) con funghi: thin-sliced button mushrooms sauteed in butter with onion and garlic, deglazed with white wine or vermouth, then tossed with thick pasta and enough starchy pasta water to make a lightly sauced, shiny dish; finished with parmigiano and parsley.
glance: 1/2 kilo (about 1 pound) stringozzi, or thick linguine or spaghetti
1 1/2 pounds white or brown button, sliced scant 1/4 inch
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the cheese and use olive oil
faq: What is stringozzi?

A thick, square-profiled noodle from Umbria, quite a bit thicker than average straight pasta, though not as thick as Tuscan pici. A 1/2 kilo (17.6 ounce) bag serves 6 hungry adults because it's unusually filling.
What can I use instead of stringozzi?
Linguine or even spaghetti, planning on a bit more per person.
What is the critical step?

The final minute of cooking the pasta together with the mushrooms: add enough pasta cooking water to deglaze the pan and develop a bit of sauce. If served dry ("tight" as chefs say) it will be bland and chewy; there should be a little shine.
Will pasta water dilute the sauce?
No. It is already seasoned with salt and has some body from the starch the noodles shed, so in small quantities it won't be watery. Add it a little at a time; you probably won't need all of it.
What can I use instead of white wine?
Dry vermouth works well and has a different flavor the author finds appealing.
Do cultivated mushrooms work?
Yes. Living in Seattle with wild mushrooms around, the author notes he sometimes forgets how delicious cultivated button mushrooms can be.

summary: Polenta with pan-roasted porcini, tomato confit and chevre: porcini halves seared cut-side down in olive oil, served over creamy polenta with oven-roasted tomato confit (about 3 hours at 300°F) and fresh chevre; serves 4.
glance: 8-12 good-sized, halved lengthwise, seared hot to caramelize a crust
20 plum tomato halves, roasted about 3 hours at 300°F (makes double)
pressure cooker method with Parmesan, milk and butter
faq: How do you cook porcini so they're the star?

Don't cut them up small. Give them a fast, hot sear in olive oil, cut side down without moving them much, until well browned, then flip, season and brown the rounded side, developing a bit of a caramelized crust.
How do you make tomato confit?

Peel plum tomatoes (a few seconds in boiling water), halve and seed them, place cut side up on a lined baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, salt, garlic, thyme and tarragon, and roast at 300°F, turning the pan occasionally, about 3 hours until flat and much of the liquid is gone.
Is the tomato confit worth making in quantity?
The recipe makes double what's needed. The author says to master the method since confit makes a great addition to pasta, risotto, soup and bruschetta.
How does the author make polenta?

With the basic pressure cooker method from Hip Pressure Cooking, adding plenty of grated Parmesan, milk and butter. It's less work and comes out perfectly creamy, as good as stovetop, though a traditional method also works. Make extra and fry the leftovers the next day.
Where do I find fresh porcini?
They are one of nature's great treats and expensive unless you forage; the author hopes to learn to forage someday.

summary: Warm frisee salad with brown butter vinaigrette: turnip half-moons and mushrooms browned in butter, garlic cooked 30 seconds, then frisee and champagne or sherry vinegar tossed in the butter about 30 seconds and served with toasted hazelnuts; serves 4 in 15 minutes.
glance: 4 tablespoons, browned lightly and nutty (lower the heat at the first sign of burning)
1/2 cup toasted hazelnuts and black pepper
faq: Why a warm salad?

Warm salads seem more filling than cold ones, and a bit special, and are nice in cool weather especially if you aren't serving a soup. Classic versions use bacon and its fat; this one uses brown butter and caramelized turnips for that rich flavor and texture.
How do I brown butter without burning it?
Brown it lightly until it develops a nutty aroma and is infused with the flavors of turnip and mushroom. At the first sign of overcooking, lower the heat to medium-low or even low.
How do I turn it into a meal?
Top with a poached or fried egg and serve with slices of toasted artisanal bread.
What else can I add?
Toasted walnut or pecan halves and shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano are also delicious.
How long do I wilt the frisee?
Turn off the heat, add the frisee, vinegar and a bit more salt and toss in the butter just enough to barely begin to wilt, about 30 seconds, then lift out with tongs, shaking off excess butter.

summary: Lentil and cucumber salad for potlucks and picnics: cucumbers salted and drained about 30 minutes, 1 pound of lentils simmered to tender and rinsed cold, tossed with red onion, olive oil, lemon, dill and mint; makes a big potluck-sized bowl (halve it for a family).
glance: a big potluck-sized bowl; cut in half for regular family use
2 English, salted and drained about 30 minutes
1 pound, simmered until tender but not mushy and rinsed in cold water
a day ahead, but add the herbs and final adjustments close to serving
faq: How do I keep cucumbers from making the salad watery?

Cucumbers leak juice that dilutes the dressing. Salt them with 1 tablespoon of kosher salt and drain in a colander over a bowl for about half an hour, weighted if you can, until translucent; rinse and pat dry. It also gives them a nicer flavor and texture.
How do I cook the lentils?

Sort and rinse, cover with a couple of inches of water, bring to a boil and simmer until tender but not mushy, then immediately drain and rinse in several changes of cold water. Stop too soon and they have an unpleasant snap; go too long and you've made lentil soup.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes, a day ahead, but re-toss it and check whether you need to drain off a bit of liquid. Hold off on the herbs and the final flavor adjustment until close to serving time.
What lentils did the author use?
Zero-tannin Shasta lentils from PNW Co-Op, which give a beautiful pale color; ChefShop.com sells them. If not available, a regular lentil will do.
Any additions?
Try some Dijon mustard in the dressing; it is friendly with dill and lemon juice.

summary: Tiny eggplant and okra in tamarind sauce: tiny eggplants quartered through the base, rubbed with ground spices and roasted at 450°F for about 30 minutes, then served on an okra, onion and tomato sauce simmered with tamarind, amchoor and kaffir lime leaves; serves 4.
glance: 8 tiny (about 3 inches long), roasted at 450°F about 30 minutes
simmer about 10 minutes with tamarind, amchoor and kaffir lime leaves
faq: What are kaffir lime leaves and what can I substitute?

They produce an amazingly floral citrus scent and aren't always easy to source; try a well-stocked Asian or Indian grocery. There really is no substitute, but a little lime zest is as close as you can come.
What is amchoor?
Dried mango powder, available at Indian groceries, which adds sour-fruity tang to the sauce.
How do you prepare the tiny eggplants?

Cut each into 4 segments lengthwise leaving the stem intact, rub all cut surfaces with a ground spice, salt and oil mixture, and roast in a single layer in a casserole until thoroughly tender, about 30 minutes. It's fun to eat most with a fork and then pick up the stem to get the last bit.
Can I leave out the okra?
Yes, if you're okra-negative. The author likes okra even a little slimy, and suggests toasted crushed peanuts on top.
What do I serve with it?
Saffron basmati rice, raita, papadum and lime pickle for an Indian meal, or omit the tomato and go Thai or Malaysian with jasmine or sticky rice.
How do I assemble and finish?
Move the okra and sauce into the hot casserole, set the eggplant on top and return to the oven about 5 minutes until bubbling, then add black pepper, finishing salt and cilantro.

summary: Rustic peach and nectarine crostata, a free-form pie: a flaky dough of 2 cups flour and 12 tablespoons very cold butter chilled at least an hour, rolled to a 13-inch round, filled with fruit leaving a 1.5-inch rim, sugared and baked 40-50 minutes at 400°F; serves 4-6.
glance: chill at least 1 hour and up to 2 days
400°F for about 40-50 minutes, until the crust is golden brown
4-5 large ripe peaches and/or nectarines, 10-12 slices each
faq: What is a crostata?
Pie without the fuss: a rustic free-form tart. It takes the author's inability to make a precise pie and makes a rustic virtue of it. You can use just about any fruit that suits your mood.
How do I make a tender, flaky crust?

Use really cold butter and water, work the butter into the flour only 1 to 2 minutes, add only enough water to form a shaggy mass, work the dough just enough to form a ball, refrigerate before rolling and let it warm back up slightly. The goal is well-distributed pockets of butter that separate the layers while minimizing gluten.
How much water does the dough need?

Start with 1/4 cup ice water and add more a couple of teaspoons at a time until you can form a big shaggy ball. Err on the side of minimal water; the amount depends on the moisture in your flour and butter.
What tool is best for the butter?
The author prefers a pastry blender, since his hands are too warm and dirtying a whole food processor makes more work than necessary.
How do I roll out the dough?

Let it warm 5 to 20 minutes until slightly pliable, give it several thwacks with a rolling pin, roll from the center out, rotating, to about 13 inches, transfer to a lined baking sheet and refrigerate 15 minutes before filling.
How do I assemble it?

Arrange the fruit slices in rings or randomly leaving a 1.5-inch rim, roll the rim up around the fruit, brush the rim with melted butter and drizzle the rest on the fruit, sprinkle brown sugar on the fruit and white or sanding sugar on the pastry.

summary: Huevos ahogados ("drowned eggs"): four eggs poached directly in simmering tomatillo salsa verde (or tomato broth) for about 3 minutes in a covered pot, served with soft corn tortillas to wipe the bowl clean; serves 2.
glance: 3 cups tomatillo salsa, about the consistency of tomato soup
cover and cook 3 minutes, then check the whites every minute
faq: What does huevos ahogados mean?
Drowned eggs: the eggs have just been poached directly in a thin salsa, a simple Mexican egg dish. The runny yolk mixes with the sauce and you wipe it all up with soft corn tortillas.
What salsa should I use?
A tomatillo salsa verde, a tomato broth like Senor Moose in Seattle uses, or a jarred salsa, pureed if chunky and thinned to about the consistency of typical tomato soup.
How do I poach the eggs in the salsa?

Bring the salsa to a simmer in a small saucepan with a lid, crack each egg carefully right above the sauce, pull the shell halves apart and let it nestle in, cover and cook 3 minutes, then check and keep checking every minute until no transparent white remains.
Is it hard to poach eggs this way?
No. If you've had trouble poaching eggs it won't be a problem: the salsa has enough body to keep the whites in a compact ball around the yolks.
Is it good for a hangover?
The author states the obvious: it is great hangover food.

summary: Spanish green olive tapenade for crostini: a cup of pitted green olives (soaked in hot water 5 minutes to remove some salt) pulsed in a food processor with roasted red or piquillo peppers, orange zest and juice, chili flakes and smoked paprika; makes 1 cup.
glance: about 5 minutes soak plus a minute in the food processor
green olives, orange zest, smoked paprika
faq: Why soak the olives?
One small trick: soak olives in hot water for a few minutes to remove some of the saltiness. You can do the same with black olives or capers in similar recipes.
Is it better as a dip or a topping?
This tapenade is on the thicker side and works better as a crostini or bruschetta topping than as a dip.
What gives it Spanish flavors?
Green olives, orange zest and juice, and smoked paprika (pimenton dulce), plus roasted red peppers, preferably piquillo.
How coarse should it be?
Pulse in a food processor until it holds together but is still somewhat coarse, then taste and check the seasoning.
Where did the recipe come from?
It's the second of three crostini toppings the author made for a Kavana Men Cook event.

summary: Delicata squash stuffed with orzo in a sage brown butter sauce, a vegetarian Thanksgiving entree: roasted squash halves filled with orzo, pepitas and dried cranberries tossed in sage-infused brown butter and lemon, topped with breadcrumbs, reheated and garnished with pomegranate; 45 minutes, serves 4.
glance: 4 as an entree (half a squash each)
assemble a day or two ahead; add pepitas just before heating to keep them crunchy
Vegetarian; vegan with olive oil; gluten-free with gluten-free pasta and no breadcrumbs
faq: Why delicata squash?

It's relatively small, and the peel is delicate and edible, so it's nice to work with. Half a squash is a perfect entree size, a quarter a good side dish. If you can't find it, use acorn or any other winter squash.
How do I make brown butter?

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and keep it cooking until it develops a nutty, caramel aroma and light brown color, about 5 minutes. Taste carefully; it should have a caramel flavor, otherwise it isn't cooked long enough. Tear in sage leaves while hot and steep, then strain.
Can I make it ahead?

Yes. Do most of it a day or two ahead and just heat and garnish. Even better, make the orzo mixture without the pepitas and fill the squash and add pepitas just before heating so they retain their crunch.
How do I reheat the stuffed squash?
Sprinkle on a good layer of breadcrumbs (homemade, not panko) and heat in the oven; from cold, start covered with foil and remove it for the last few minutes.
Is the recipe precise?
The author guesstimated amounts for 16 portions without writing them down, so it isn't precise but is close enough to fine-tune. Despite 12 steps, it goes together pretty quickly.
What can I do with leftover brown butter?
Try it on popcorn or brussels sprouts.

summary: Mushroom risotto with asparagus and fava beans: a pound of finely chopped mushrooms cooked about 20 minutes like a duxelles, stirred into arborio rice cooked with white wine and water (stovetop, or 5 1/2 minutes in a pressure cooker), finished with butter and Parmigiano; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound, finely chopped in a food processor, cooked about 20 minutes until dry
2 cups arborio, 1 cup white wine and 5 cups simmering water
4 cups water, high pressure 5 minutes 30 seconds
faq: Why use water instead of broth?

To allow the mushroom flavor to shine. The risotto gets its intensity from a whole pound of finely chopped mushrooms sauteed in olive oil until they give up all their liquid, similar to the French method for duxelles.
How do I peel fava beans easily?

Remove the outer pod, freeze the beans, and thaw them the next day: that loosens the skin so you pinch off a bit and squeeze and they pop out. The freeze/thaw also makes the bean more tender because ice crystals break cell walls, which Ideas in Food calls cryo-blanching; the beans don't need cooking.
What does all'onda mean?
Wavy, the classic Venetian style of quite wet risotto. The Piedmontese style is a bit more firm. The author's photo was too dry and he'd add a bit more liquid.
What is mantecare?
Mixing in butter and Parmigiano at the end to add a final dose of creaminess, which the author highly recommends however you make risotto.
How do I make it in a pressure cooker?

Saute the rice 2 minutes, stir in the wine until it evaporates, add the mushrooms and 4 cups of water, cook at high pressure 5 minutes 30 seconds, release the pressure quickly, and check a grain for al dente. If still too firm, cook a little more without pressure and add 30 seconds next time.
When is the rice done?
When it is fully tender but still has a slight al dente resistance, but absolutely not a snap.
